question: Is reasoning_effort quality worth the output tokens, and is the advisor `medium` raise justified?
method: 6 planning/orchestration tasks (experiments/e08b-t1..t6: plan, delegation brief w/ child cap, debug triage, cost judgment, 3-way choice, verify-before-reporting) x effort low/medium/high x 2 runs x 2 models = 72 runs, all --oneshot --ignore-rules, no tools. Graded by openai/gpt-6-luna (non-candidate), 6 batched grader calls with anonymized shuffled answers. Per-run override only, no config changes.
verdict: No effort level buys a clear quality win on these tasks. Pass counts show no consistent low<medium<high trend for either model (deepseek peaks at medium 7/12 then drops to 3/12 at high; kimi low and medium tie at 5). Raising effort does not even save tokens: kimi at LOW is its most verbose (mean 1,079 out). Deepseek delivers a similar pass rate at ~8.6x lower cost per passed task ($0.0015 vs $0.0129). Caveats: n=2 runs/cell, single grader pass, rubric is strict (task 3 debug triage failed for every cell — likely grader strictness, not model failure), letter-parse of grader output is approximate. Treat as indicative, not publishable-grade.
recommendation: Keep reasoning_effort low on main AND advisor. The advisor medium raise (F6) is unproven by this data — no pass-rate gain anywhere to justify it; revert or leave with no further changes. Delegation, not effort, remains the lever for 'smarter'.
